chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to exchange one qafiz of wheat for two qafiz of barley?' He said, 'It is not permissible except like for like.' Then he said, 'Barley is from wheat.'

key_terms.قَفِيزٌ: A traditional unit of volume measurement used for dry goods.
key_terms.مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ: Like for like; equal in measure and quality, a key condition in barter.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging different quantities of similar food grains in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that exchanging one qafiz of wheat for two qafiz of barley is impermissible because they are of the same commodity type (wheat and barley), requiring an equal measure (mithlan bi-mithl) in barter transactions to avoid riba (usury). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that wheat and barley are classified under the same genus for the purpose of *riba al-fadl*, ensuring that any excess in quantity is prohibited when the exchange is immediate. The emphasis on 'mithlan bi-mithl' underscores the importance of equality in kind to prevent hidden interest in spot trades of staple foods.
